nodes.name: Micelle assembly reduction
nodes.procedure: 10 mg of the diblock copolymer was dissolved in 1.5 mL of N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) to form a clear solution, which was then divided into five equal portions. Each portion received 0.8 mL of a Pt (40 mM)/Pd (40 mM)/Ru (80 mM)/Mo (120 mM)/Rh (60 mM) metal salt solution, inducing micellization with hydrophilic PEO shells and hydrophobic PS cores that retained metal ions. The portions were combined and stirred for 2 h, followed by the addition of 0.3 mL of 6 M hydrochloric acid to adjust the pH. After 30 min of further stirring, the mixture was transferred to a preheated oil bath at 95°C. There, 3 mL of formic acid was introduced as a reducing agent, and the reaction proceeded for 2 h. The final product was collected by centrifugation (12,000 rpm, 25 min) and washed with acetone, ethanol, and water to remove residual copolymers.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Mesoporous HEA Samples. Mesoporous PtPdRhRuMo HEA nanoparticles [m-HEANP(Mo)] were synthesized via micelle assembly using polystyrene-b-poly(ethylene oxide) (PS5000-b-PEO2500) and a wet-chemical method.

nodes.name: Soft-templated electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: 4 mg of the diblock copolymer was dissolved in 0.6 mL of THF. Subsequently, 0.5 mL of ethanol, 2.32 mL of deionized water, and 0.08 mL of 2 M HCl were added to form a micellar solution at 40°C. A sequential addition of 0.1 mL each of K2PtCl4 (40 mM), Na2PdCl4 (40 mM), Na3RhCl6 (40 mM), RuCl3·xH2O (40 mM), and MoCl5 (40 mM) was performed to introduce metal precursors into the electrolyte. Electrodeposition was conducted using a conventional three-electrode setup, comprising a Pt wire counter electrode, an Ag/AgCl reference electrode (in 3 M KCl), and an Au-coated Si wafer (3×15 mm) as the working electrode. The m-HEAF(Mo) was deposited electrochemically at a constant potential of -0.2 V (vs Ag/AgCl) for 300 s. Following deposition, the working electrode was immersed in THF at room temperature for 24 h to remove the micellar template.
nodes.source_text: Similarly, the mesoporous HEA film [m-HEAF(Mo)] was synthesized by dissolving 4 mg of the diblock copolymer in 0.6 mL of THF.

nodes.evidence_snippet: the scanning electron microscopy (SEM)... images reveal the mesoporous features of m-HEANP(Mo) nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images reveal mesoporous features and enable EDS mapping for m-HEANP(Mo) nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images reveal the mesoporous features of m-HEANP(Mo) nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping confirms uniform elemental distribution of Pt, Pd, Ru, Rh, Mo in m-HEANP(Mo) nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) in HAADF-STEM mode is used to visualize the elemental distribution profile... confirming the uniform distribution of constituent Pt, Pd, Ru, Rh, and Mo elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD pattern exhibits characteristic peaks identical to Pt (JCPDS 03-065-2868) confirming single-phase fcc structure with lattice constant 0.392 nm for m-HEANP(Mo).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern exhibits characteristic peaks identical to those of the Pt system (JCPDS card No. 03-065-2868), confirming that the m-HEANP(Mo) nanoparticles crystallize in a single-phase fcc structure (Figure 4e). The lattice constant determined from the XRD pattern was 0.392 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Valence band spectrum shows featureless profile indicating entropy-driven electronic structure modification compared to monometallic Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the valence band (VB) spectrum was examined by using hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (HAXPES, Cr Kα source)... the featureless VB spectrum of m-HEANP(Mo), in contrast to the monometallic Pt system, reflects entropy-driven modifications.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals mesoporous structural integrity throughout m-HEAF(Mo) film.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The cross-sectional TEM analysis of focused ion beam (FIB)-prepared specimens revealed mesoporous structural integrity throughout m-HEAF(Mo).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes with interplanar spacing of 0.226 nm corresponding to fcc (111) plane for m-HEAF(Mo).
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) showed lattice fringes with an interplanar spacing of 0.226 nm, corresponding to the (111) plane of the fcc structure (Figure 4h).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern confirms fcc structure of m-HEAF(Mo).
STEM-EDS mapping and line-scan confirm spatial uniformity of Pt, Pd, Rh, Ru, Mo across m-HEAF(Mo) mesoporous film.
nodes.evidence_snippet: elemental homogeneity was verified through STEM-EDS mapping, with line-scan profiles demonstrating spatial uniformity of all constituent metals.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of m-HEAF(Mo) show fcc Pt peaks shifted to higher angles compared to m-MEAF indicating lattice shrinkage from Mo incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD analysis of both the m-MEAF and m-HEAF(Mo) samples exhibited distinct characteristic peaks corresponding to the fcc structure of Pt... Compared to m-MEAF, the diffraction peaks of m-HEAF(Mo) shift toward higher angles, indicating lattice shrinkage due to the incorporation of smaller Mo atoms (Figure 4k).

nodes.characterization_summary: Wide-scan XPS shows intense characteristic peaks of Pt, Pd, Ru, Rh, Mo confirming multi-elemental high-entropy character of m-HEANP(Mo).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The multi-elemental character of the m-HEANP(Mo) exterior is also evident from the intense characteristic peaks of Pt, Pd, Ru, Rh, and Mo in the wide-scan X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectrum.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRXPS Pt 4f shows negative shift in binding energy indicating electron-rich Pt from charge transfer, more pronounced in higher-Mo m-HEAF(Mo).
nodes.evidence_snippet: high-resolution XPS (HRXPS...) analysis on the Pt 4f core levels indicates a noticeable negative shift in the Pt 4f binding energy of both m-HEAF(Mo) and m-HEANP(Mo) compared to Pt-C.

nodes.evidence_snippet: the atomic ratio of Pt/Pd/Rh/Ru/Mo in m-HEANP(Mo) was determined to be 59/17/20/2/2 by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES, Table S5)
